debutant.name: The Mirror
debutant.desc: Two players face each other. One leads slow movements, the other mirrors perfectly. Speed up gradually.

debutant.name: Yes, and...
debutant.desc: Every offer is accepted and built upon. The golden rule of improv: never block.

debutant.name: Word at a time
debutant.desc: In a circle, each player adds one word. Build a story together without hesitating.

debutant.name: Freeze
debutant.desc: Two players improvise from a posture. Anyone can clap to freeze, replace a player, and restart the scene.

debutant.name: Emotional rollercoaster
debutant.desc: Moderator shouts an emotion every minute. Players shift their tone instantly.

debutant.name: Invisible object
debutant.desc: One player handles an invisible object. Others must guess and add new uses.

debutant.name: Three characters
debutant.desc: Three players enter and establish their character within 30 seconds via posture and voice.

debutant.name: Question circle
debutant.desc: One player in the middle. Others bombard them with rapid-fire questions to be answered precisely.

debutant.name: Mixed
debutant.desc: All troupe members play the theme together, no team split. (Adapted match category)

debutant.name: Compared
debutant.desc: Two subgroups of the troupe play the same proposition in succession. The 2nd version must differ from the 1st. (Adapted match category)

debutant.name: With prop
debutant.desc: An imposed object must be central to the collective improvisation. The whole troupe makes it work on stage. (Adapted match category)

debutant.name: Free
debutant.desc: Two subgroups play the same theme in succession with no form constraint. Total freedom. (Adapted match category)

debutant.name: The chairs
debutant.desc: One team has 30s to build a structure out of chairs. Another team has 40s to prepare an improv based on that structure. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: The eulogy
debutant.desc: Each player improvises a tribute speech for their pet. Solemn tone, funny, or both. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: Embody the theme
debutant.desc: The group is in motion; a leader calls out a theme (museum, pyramids...). The group instantly recreates it. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: Weird conversation
debutant.desc: Two players improvise an offbeat situation: a bird explaining a tree to another bird, a flea arguing with a dog. (Tadam Impro)

debutant.name: The drunk guy
debutant.desc: An audience member (or actor) plays the « drunk guy » who interrupts the scene with absurd suggestions the improvisers must work in to push the story forward.

debutant.name: The human machine
debutant.desc: One by one, players enter and add a repetitive gesture/sound. The machine builds itself organically.

debutant.name: ABC
debutant.desc: A scene where each line begins with the next letter of the alphabet. A, B, C... up to Z.

debutant.name: The bus
debutant.desc: A bus stop. With each arrival a new character boards with their own universe. The scene mutates every time.

debutant.name: Pantomime
debutant.desc: A scene played entirely in mime from a given theme. (Dramaction)

debutant.name: Passing emotion
debutant.desc: A player silently transmits an emotion to their neighbour through a gesture, who passes it on in turn. (Dramaction)

debutant.name: Beginning-middle-end in 30s
debutant.desc: Start an impro, shift the stakes, and wrap it up — all in 30 seconds flat. (Impro-Exo)

debutant.name: Shifting-emotion conversation
debutant.desc: A two-person conversation. Every 1-2 minutes a leader shouts an emotion. The players shift instantly. (MentorShow)

confirme.name: Pause-Resume
confirme.desc: Moderator stops the scene, changes one element (place, era, status), and restarts.

confirme.name: Three forced words
confirme.desc: Three random words must be naturally placed in the scene.

confirme.name: Status game
confirme.desc: Each character has a hidden social status (1 to 10). Audience must guess.

confirme.name: Dubbing
confirme.desc: Two mime, two others speak for them from offstage.

confirme.name: Expert panel
confirme.desc: Panel of experts on an absurd topic answers audience questions earnestly.

confirme.name: Last word, first word
confirme.desc: Each line begins with the last word of the previous line.

confirme.name: Reverse story
confirme.desc: Tell the story starting from the ending and moving backwards.

confirme.name: Mixed genres
confirme.desc: Moderator switches genre every 30 seconds (western, noir, romance, horror...).

confirme.name: In the manner of
confirme.desc: Everyone plays the theme in an imposed author or genre style: Shakespeare, film noir, Audiard... (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: Silent
confirme.desc: No word spoken — only the collective staging tells the story. Extreme focus. (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: Silent with music
confirme.desc: Silent improv, but the writing is rigorously influenced by the imposed musical ambience. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Forced constraint
confirme.desc: Two subgroups play the same theme in succession, each with a different constraint drawn at random. (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: No theme, no caucus
confirme.desc: No theme announced, no preparation time. Pure immediate invention. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Leapfrog
confirme.desc: Four different impros, one theme each. The 1st with one player, one is added at each subsequent impro. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Sensory
confirme.desc: One of the five senses of an improviser is stimulated during the scene. That sensation must drive the whole writing. (Dramaction)

confirme.name: Compared in the manner of
confirme.desc: Two subgroups of the troupe play the same theme in succession in the imposed style, each in their own way. (Adapted match category)

confirme.name: Triple status
confirme.desc: Each character has a secret, a goal, and an obstacle. All three are revealed during the scene.

confirme.name: Reversed scene
confirme.desc: Start at the climax and work back to the moment the characters first meet.

confirme.name: The off-key choir
confirme.desc: A choir onstage — one member is off-key or out of rhythm. The whole drama comes from them. (Wikiversité)

confirme.name: Actors backstage
confirme.desc: A scene plays out backstage while the « show » is happening onstage. Mise en abyme. (Wikiversité)

confirme.name: The broken elevator
confirme.desc: Ultra-cramped space, several characters, forced confinement. A classic. (Wikiversité)

confirme.name: The teachers' meeting
confirme.desc: A staff meeting where each teacher has a hidden agenda and a favourite pupil.

confirme.name: Back to the past
confirme.desc: At a key moment, a player claps. The scene rewinds one minute and replays differently.

confirme.name: Drawn character
confirme.desc: Each player draws a character type (clown, seducer, paranoiac) and must play it without naming it.

expert.name: The Harold
expert.desc: Long form: three parallel scenes weave and feed each other. Del Close format.

expert.name: Sung improvisation
expert.desc: Fully sung scene with improvised melody, rhymes and verse/chorus structure.

expert.name: Twenty-minute one-shot
expert.desc: Single 20-minute scene, no breaks, no resets. Hold an entire world.

expert.name: Pirandello mirror
expert.desc: Characters realize they are improvised, but must continue the scene anyway.

expert.name: Two timelines
expert.desc: Scene plays out, then replays ten years later with the consequences.

expert.name: Silent show
expert.desc: 15-minute spectacle with no dialogue at all. Clear plot, real resolution.

expert.name: Theatre within theatre
expert.desc: Characters improvise their own play inside the main scene. Three layers of fiction.

expert.name: Beckettian
expert.desc: Long-form absurd: lived silences, waiting, language emptying out. Godot-style.

expert.name: Sung
expert.desc: Improvisation entirely or partially sung by the whole troupe, improvised melodies and lyrics in collective. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Rhymed
expert.desc: All lines rhyme. Octosyllables or alexandrines per level. The whole troupe holds the meter. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Videoway
expert.desc: Mixed with four TV channels (F1-F4), different content per channel. The host jumps between channels with no pre-defined order. (Dramaction)

expert.name: Thesis
expert.desc: The collective improvisation must defend a philosophical thesis announced in advance.

expert.name: Compared sung
expert.desc: Two subgroups of the troupe successively offer their sung version of the same theme. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: Compared rhymed
expert.desc: Two subgroups of the troupe successively deliver their rhymed version of the theme. (Adapted match category)

expert.name: The Fireball
expert.desc: All players onstage. At each high beat, a duo breaks out for a mini-scene, then returns to the group.

expert.name: Shared monologue
expert.desc: A long monologue is picked up by each player, who distorts and enriches it while staying the same character.

expert.name: Improvised opera
expert.desc: Sung recitatives and arias in alternation, fully improvised libretto, operatic voices.

expert.name: The House (Del Close)
expert.desc: Long form where each scene opens themes that following scenes pick up and deepen.

expert.name: The Deconstructed
expert.desc: A single scene is played, then taken apart and restarted from several narrative angles.

expert.name: Chekhovian
expert.desc: Long-form Chekhov style: no climax, characters who miss each other, inaction as the engine.

debutant.name: Single team
debutant.desc: One team plays, the other waits. Classic LNI match form.

debutant.name: Mixed
debutant.desc: Both teams play together in the same improvisation.

debutant.name: Compared
debutant.desc: Each team performs the same prompt in turn. Audience compares and votes.

debutant.name: Mixed silent
debutant.desc: Both teams together, but in absolute silence.

debutant.name: Compared sung
debutant.desc: Each team includes at least one sung passage.

debutant.name: Compared with prop
debutant.desc: An imposed prop must be central. Each team uses it in its own way.

confirme.name: In the manner of
confirme.desc: Style or genre imposed: Shakespeare, film noir, Coen Brothers...

confirme.name: Mixed with prop
confirme.desc: An imposed object must be central to the improvisation.

confirme.name: Reverse improvisation
confirme.desc: Team must play starting from the ending.

confirme.name: Compared rhymed
confirme.desc: All lines must rhyme.

confirme.name: Compared silent
confirme.desc: No words: only gesture and expression tell the story.

confirme.name: Mixed with character
confirme.desc: An imposed character type must appear in the first minute.

confirme.name: Compared with constraint
confirme.desc: Each team plays the theme with a different randomly-drawn constraint.

confirme.name: Mixed in full sentences
confirme.desc: Players may only speak in whole, complete sentences — no interrupting.

expert.name: Sung & danced
expert.desc: Mini-musical: alternating dialogue, song and choreography, all improvised.

expert.name: Style + era
expert.desc: Both an authorial style and a historical era are imposed. Both must read clearly.

expert.name: Mixed in verse
expert.desc: All lines in verse (iambic pentameter or alexandrines).

expert.name: Heroless
expert.desc: Improvisation must work without an identifiable lead. Pure ensemble.

expert.name: Thesis improv
expert.desc: Improvisation must defend a philosophical thesis announced beforehand.

expert.name: Time loop
expert.desc: Scene moves forward then rewinds 30 seconds, repeatedly. Vertiginous loop.

expert.name: Compared silent + sound effects
expert.desc: One team plays silently, the other only with sound effects. Same theme, opposite readings.

expert.name: In the manner of Chekhov
expert.desc: Late-19th-century Russian style: aristocratic ennui, samovars, loaded silences, monologues.

debutant: Walking in a circle the entire time
Every other line must be sung
confirme: In the style of 1940s film noir
In slow motion from start to finish
In fast forward from start to finish
Alternating English and an invented language
In the style of an animated cartoon
expert: Time-rewind: scene moves forward then rewinds every 30s
Multiple voices: each character played by 2 actors at once
External narration that contradicts the action
Palindromic: scene must be playable in reverse
An entirely invented but consistent language

debutant: With a forced phrase to slip in
expert: With a character who knows it is fiction

debutant: The TV news from another planet
An interrogation about a tiny matter
confirme: A cat speaking to its owner
The train journey with no destination
The hotel forgotten by all maps
The dream that returns every night
Two strangers in a stuck elevator
The photo we shouldn't have seen
The house that changes at night

The teachers' meeting about one student
The lesson that makes no sense
Darth Vader calls to break up
expert: The final conversation between God and Devil
The testament of a dead language
The final performance at the Globe
The seven deadly sins at dinner
The dream within the dream within the dream
The tightrope walker between two worlds
Three sisters who'll never reach Moscow
The night watchman of forgotten things
The last translator of the useless

categories.name: Mixed
categories.desc: Both teams play together, balanced numbers, on the same theme.

categories.name: Compared
categories.desc: Each team plays the same prompt in turn. Audience compares and votes.

categories.name: In the manner of
categories.desc: Style or genre imposed (Shakespeare, noir, Tarantino...).

categories.name: Compared in the manner of
categories.desc: Each team plays the theme in the imposed style, in its own way.

categories.name: Compared sung
categories.desc: Each team offers its own sung version of the same theme.

categories.name: Silent
categories.desc: No spoken word: only gesture tells the story.

categories.name: Silent with music
categories.desc: Mute scene, but writing rigorously shaped by an imposed musical mood.

categories.name: Rhymed
categories.desc: All lines must rhyme. Couplets or alexandrines depending on level.

categories.name: Compared rhymed
categories.desc: Each team delivers its own rhymed version of the theme.

categories.name: With prop
categories.desc: An imposed object must be central.

categories.name: Forced constraint
categories.desc: A constraint drawn at random applies to one or both teams.

categories.name: No theme, no caucus
categories.desc: No theme announced, no preparation time. Pure on-the-spot invention.

categories.name: Leapfrog
categories.desc: Four different improvs, one theme each. The first with one player; one player added each round.

categories.name: Videoway
categories.desc: Mixed with 4 TV channels (F1-F4), different content per channel. Referee jumps between channels at will.

categories.name: Sensory
categories.desc: One sense of one improviser is stimulated. That sensation must shape the entire scene.

categories.name: Thesis
categories.desc: Improvisation must defend a philosophical thesis announced in advance.

categories.name: Free
categories.desc: No formal constraint, just the theme. Total freedom of treatment.
